clue.text: Significant number grumpy when Conservative's got away with inclusion of rejected line

indicators.note: the shortened word for grumpy takes the next piece inside it
the Conservative has got away, so that letter leaves the word for grumpy

parts.note: tetchy means irritable or grumpy
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: a rejected item is sent back, so the word for line is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A grumpy politician leaves after a disputed line is struck out of a major report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got away' drops C from TETCHY to leave TETHY; 'rejected' turns ROW into WOR, and 'with inclusion of' puts WOR inside TETHY after its TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth taking note of is significant or remarkable.

clue.text: Start with conclusion first? Certainly not

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for start is brought round to the front

parts.note: to open something is to start it

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks whether to begin at the end and is firmly refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with conclusion first' takes the last letter N of OPEN and moves it to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A slangy flat refusal, an informal no.

clue.text: Haulage organisation with European flag

parts.note: TIR (Transports Internationaux Routiers) is the international road haulage system whose plates appear on lorries

explanation.surface: A continental trucking body adopts a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: TIR is seen on the back of European lorries crossing borders under the international customs transit scheme. 'Flag' here is the verb, to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or grow weary, which is to tire.

clue.text: Ride out to catch thief miserably showing mark of cowardice

indicators.note: the word for ride out holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to ride out a storm is to weather it

indicators.note: done miserably, the letters of thief are put in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A rider sets off after a thief but shows himself a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' rearranges THIEF to HITEF, and 'to catch' puts that inside WEATHER after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: In British tradition a white feather was handed to men thought to be cowards, so it marks cowardice.

clue.text: One embraced by Romeo induced upset

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to lead someone into something is to induce them, so induced gives led
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone hugged by Romeo ends up upset, as in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts I inside R + LED, between R and LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means angered or annoyed, upset in the sense of being put out.

clue.text: A good king, in secret, tormented

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the word for secret

parts.note: something secret is hidden
R (rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A virtuous monarch, kept in hiding, suffers torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A + G + R inside HIDDEN, after its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hag-ridden means harassed or plagued, as if ridden by a witch at night.

clue.text: Bit of solemnity joker spoils

indicators.note: a small bit of the word solemnity is its first letter

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A joker's touch of seriousness ruins the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a verb but is the noun, loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is stolen goods or booty, the spoils of a crime.

clue.text: Dealer in pickle and salt reported

indicators.note: reported speech, so the two words are said out loud to give the sound of another word

parts.note: a pickle is a predicament, a hole; a salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A trader in preserved goods and seasoning gets mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' and 'salt' look like groceries, but mean a tight spot (a hole) and an old seaman (a sailor). HOLE SAILOR spoken sounds like the trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler is a trader who sells goods in bulk to retailers, a dealer.

clue.text: Reptile nearly uncovered under assortment of rags on ship

indicators.note: in a down answer the last piece is placed below the others
an assortment mixes things up, so the letters of rags are rearranged

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: uncovered means naked

explanation.surface: A snake lies nearly bare beneath a pile of rags aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment of' turns RAGS into GRAS; 'nearly' trims NAKED to NAKE, which sits 'under' GRAS + SS in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass snake is a common harmless European snake.

clue.text: A son providing ample heartless mockery

parts.note: per means a or each, as in fifty pence per item
if means providing, on condition that

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: ample means large

explanation.surface: A boy who is generous but cold is the target of mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes R, the middle letter of LARGE, leaving LAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, teasing banter, a form of gentle mockery.

clue.text: Trouble with chapter coming about in final section

indicators.note: coming about is a sailing term for turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Problems in one chapter lead to the conclusion of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming about' reverses ADO + C, giving CODA.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music or literature.

clue.text: Upset character, breaking silence, irritates passengers

indicators.note: the reversed piece breaks into the word for silence

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: in a down light upset means turned upside down, so the word for character is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a character in a play
angers means irritates

explanation.surface: A distressed person breaks the quiet and annoys those nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns PART into TRAP; 'breaking' puts TRAP inside SH to give STRAPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Straphangers are standing commuters holding hanging straps on trains or buses, so passengers.

clue.text: Person in charge of school, man with a gown, film covered

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: the word for gown covers the word for film

parts.note: a gown is a dress
a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: A school head appears with a man in a gown, both caught on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' places MIST inside DRESS after its D, giving DMISTRESS after HE + A.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who runs a school is its head teacher.

clue.text: Hear, around start of eulogy, quote raised concerning religious teaching

indicators.note: the word for hear goes around the next piece

parts.note: to catch something said is to hear it

indicators.note: the start of eulogy is its first letter
in a down light raised means read upwards, so the word for quote is reversed

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Listen to a eulogy, then quote it aloud at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts E inside CATCH (CATECH); 'raised' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Catechetic relates to the catechism, teaching doctrine by question and answer.

clue.text: Make chaotic threat after losing rook — is a bishop protected?

indicators.note: the shortened word for threat surrounds the further pieces as a guard
losing the rook means the letter for it is dropped from the word for threat

parts.note: a danger is a threat
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A chess threat collapses after a rook is lost; the question is whether a bishop is guarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes R from DANGER to leave DANGE, and 'protected' puts IS A RR inside it after the D. The chess picture is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarrange is to throw into disorder, to mess up.

clue.text: on item worn on head

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'on item worn on head' (5,4): its opening words are cut off, so the wordplay giving ALICE is missing; no scan or reprint found.

clue.text: Tractable after a dispute getting a sweetener

indicators.note: the word for tractable comes after the others

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
tractable means docile, tame

explanation.surface: A compliant person, after an argument, receives a sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetener' could be a bribe, but here it is the sugar substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial low-calorie sweetening agent.

clue.text: Stove fashionable once more

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron kitchen range
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A stove has come back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a large cooking range found in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a second time, anew.

clue.text: Stick around with time to play

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for stick is read backwards

parts.note: a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about with time to amuse themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses CANE to ENAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a part is to perform or act it out on stage.

clue.text: Cheap fastener beginning to buckle in test

parts.note: a pin is a fastener

indicators.note: the first letter of buckle goes inside the word for test

parts.note: a check is a test

indicators.note: the beginning of buckle is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cheap clasp begins to give way under testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside CHECK, after its CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck is a copper-zinc alloy imitating gold, so it means sham or cheap.

clue.text: Horrid agents involved in hard bargaining

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nasty agents are caught up in tough negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, tough negotiation with concessions, as when dealers sold livestock.

clue.text: Day on tropical island in loincloth

parts.note: tropical weather is hot

explanation.surface: A day spent on a hot island wearing only a loincloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhoti is a garment of cloth wrapped round the waist and legs worn by Hindu men.

clue.text: See officer getting mad

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: Notice the officer losing his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is slang for crazy.

clue.text: Good essayist's poetical works

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the phrase has the run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A fine essayist also writes verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the words, gOOD ESsayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyrical poems, so a collection of them is poetic work.

clue.text: Lean guard

explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to incline or lean towards something, and to tend a flock is to look after or guard it.

clue.text: Bit of time not available before feature by bluff director

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
a con is a bluff or trick

explanation.surface: An unavailable bluffer cannot be seen by the director for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' means a part of the face here.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a second, a tiny unit of time.

clue.text: Get about, looking hot, showing trendiness

parts.note: C (circa) means about
red is the colour of something hot, as in red-hot

explanation.surface: Getting around while looking sexy shows you are fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for street credibility, cool standing with fashionable people.

clue.text: Vegetables I spot growing wild in area of ground over behind rear of coop

indicators.note: the rest goes behind that letter
the rear of coop is its last letter
the jumbled letters sit inside the reversed word for area of ground
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a site is a plot or area of ground

indicators.note: growing wild means these letters run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peas sprout wildly in a vegetable patch behind the chicken coop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SITE into ETIS; 'growing wild' makes TSPO from spot, and with I that goes 'in' ETIS after ETI. The farmyard picture hides that 'area of ground' is a building plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits pois are small, sweet young peas, a vegetable.
